Cylinder Flow: From Spatial Fields to Equations¶

Companion exploration to the IX/Digital Foundry tutorial

Discover a symbolic evolution law for the dominant coordinates of a flow field, then reconstruct its spatial structure.

Based on Faraji and Belardinelli (2026).

Setup¶

  1. Open this notebook in Colab and select Runtime → Change runtime type → Runtime Version → 2026.07 (Python 3.12). Choose CPU for the main walkthrough.

  3. If setup asks you to restart, choose Runtime → Restart session, then rerun the setup cell. Do not choose Disconnect and delete runtime; a restart keeps the installed packages.

1. A field becomes a few temporal coordinates¶

POD separates spatial patterns from their time-dependent coefficients.

$$\omega(\mathbf r,t)\approx\bar\omega(\mathbf r)+\sum_{k=1}^{r}a_k(t)\phi_k(\mathbf r).$$

  • Fixed Reynolds number $Re=300$; $\bar\omega$ is the development mean vorticity field.
  • $\phi_k$ are spatial modes; $a_k(t)$ are their coefficients. Up to 20 modes are supplied for reconstruction.
  • Discovery uses six standardized coordinates, $z_k=(a_k-c_k)/s_k$, with development means $c_k$ and scales $s_k$ reused for validation and testing.
In [3]:
# Load the six-coordinate discovery case and its 20-mode spatial decomposition.
flow = workflow.load_cylinder(rank=6)
artifact = flow["artifact"]
mode_energies = artifact["singular_values"]**2
energy_fraction = np.cumsum(mode_energies) / artifact["total_training_fluctuation_energy"]
retained_modes = np.array([4, 6, 10, 20])
display(pd.DataFrame({
    "Modes": retained_modes,
    "Development fluctuation energy (%)": 100 * energy_fraction[retained_modes - 1],
}))
figures.rank_reconstruction(flow)
plt.show()
Modes Development fluctuation energy (%)
0 4 85.608584
1 6 94.516795
2 10 98.715228
3 20 99.903634

These reconstructions use the same development mean and basis and share one color scale. The included data provide all 20 development coefficients and validation/test coefficients for three through six modes.

Increasing reconstruction rank is distinct from increasing the dimension of the symbolic ODE. The VG backbone supports at most six state coordinates. We use six for equation discovery, retaining three pairs of spatial modes.

2. Generate, pool, and rank in the VG workflow¶

The frozen backbone generates candidate systems from several observed windows.

  • Generate: eight five-time-unit discovery windows supply observations to ODEFormer.
  • Pool: combine distinct candidate systems.
  • Rank: compare rollouts over all 24 discovery windows and keep the ten lowest-error candidates.

A rollout is obtained by integrating the candidate from a window's initial condition. For each state coordinate and window, divide the mean squared prediction error by the observation variance—the mean squared distance of the observations from their mean. Average these NMSE values across coordinates and windows, as in the main notebook.

The data use consecutive development, validation, and test intervals. The saved pool below uses development data; we recompute two ranking scores using ODEFormer's timeout-protected integration.

In [4]:
pool = flow["pool"].sort_values("rollout_rank")
shortlist = pool.head(10).copy()
ranking_windows = flow["ranking_windows"]
generation_windows = flow["generation_windows"]
ranking_rows = []
for candidate in shortlist.head(2).itertuples():
    window_errors = []
    for window in ranking_windows:
        prediction = workflow.rollout(candidate.equation, window["t"], window["x0"])
        window_errors.append(workflow.nmse(window["x"], prediction))
    ranking_rows.append({"Candidate": candidate.candidate_id, "Discovery NMSE": np.mean(window_errors)})
display(pd.DataFrame(ranking_rows))
workflow.show_equation(shortlist.iloc[0]["equation"], name="z", title="Best-ranked raw system")

3. Verify the reduced dynamics¶

Compare the two sides of each equation and the oscillations of the reduced coordinates.

  • Derivative: numerical derivatives of observed states versus candidate expressions at those same states.
  • Oscillation: percentile amplitudes and dominant nonzero Fourier frequencies of each coordinate, rather than the peak-spacing periods used for Van der Pol.
  • Full-suite checks: bounded evolution and consistent amplitudes/frequencies from three starting states.

Candidate rollouts span 30 time units; oscillation measurements use $t\ge5$. These are the recorded experiment's prescribed intervals. Full-suite acceptance requires amplitude/frequency errors below 15%/10%, cross-start coefficients of variation below 10%/5%, and state norm below three times the largest development norm.

In [5]:
# Numerical derivatives use neighboring observations along the time axis.
observed_states = flow["train"]["x"]
observation_times = flow["train"]["t"]
observed_derivative = np.gradient(observed_states, observation_times, axis=0, edge_order=2)
derivative_scale = np.var(observed_derivative, axis=0) + 1e-12

derivative_scores = []
for equation in shortlist.equation:
    predicted_derivative = workflow.vector_field(equation, observed_states)
    squared_difference = (predicted_derivative - observed_derivative)**2
    normalized_error = np.mean(squared_difference, axis=0) / derivative_scale
    derivative_scores.append(np.mean(normalized_error))
local_limit = 2 * np.min(derivative_scores)

Apply the checks and select¶

Choose the lowest-error candidate among those passing all checks.

The complete shortlist sets the derivative threshold. Each candidate then receives the same checks.

In [6]:
verification_rows = []
for candidate in shortlist.itertuples():
    checks = workflow.verify_flow(candidate.equation, flow, local_limit)
    verification_rows.append({"candidate_id":candidate.candidate_id,
                              "rollout_rank":candidate.rollout_rank, **checks})
checked = pd.DataFrame(verification_rows)
display(checked[["candidate_id", "rollout_rank", "local", "amplitude", "frequency", "starting_states", "bounded", "verifier_admissible"]])
passing = checked.loc[checked.verifier_admissible].sort_values("rollout_rank")
if passing.empty:
    raise RuntimeError("No admissible candidate; stop before refinement.")
# First row after filtering and ordering is the accepted candidate.
selected_id = passing.iloc[0].candidate_id

4. Refine constants and verify again¶

Keep the expression structure fixed and optimize the same mean NMSE used for ranking.

For each coordinate and development window, divide the mean squared prediction error by the observation variance, then average over the six coordinates and 24 windows.

  • Load the recorded optimized coefficients and rerun the full cylinder suite.
  • Accept them if all checks pass; otherwise retain the admissible raw equation.
  • Display the complete accepted six-equation system below.
In [7]:
assert selected_id == flow["model"]["candidate_id"], "Recorded refinement belongs to a different candidate."
raw_equation = flow["model"]["initial_equation"]
refined_equation = flow["model"]["optimized_equation"]
raw_checks = workflow.verify_flow(raw_equation, flow, local_limit)
if not raw_checks["verifier_admissible"]:
    raise RuntimeError("The raw equation must pass before refinement.")
post_checks = workflow.verify_flow(refined_equation, flow, local_limit)
if post_checks["verifier_admissible"]:
    final_equation = refined_equation
    print("Refined equation accepted")
else:
    final_equation = raw_equation
    print("Raw admissible equation retained")
workflow.show_equation(final_equation, name="z", title="Accepted cylinder-flow model")

Refined equation accepted

Accepted cylinder-flow model

$$ \begin{aligned}\dot{z}_{0} &= 1.001 z_{1}- \frac{0.005089}{\left(1 - 0.07379 z_{1}\right)^{1.052}} \\[5pt] \dot{z}_{1} &= - 1.123 z_{0} \\[5pt] \dot{z}_{2} &= - 2.099 z_{3} \\[5pt] \dot{z}_{3} &= 2.12 z_{2} \\[5pt] \dot{z}_{4} &= 3.121 z_{5}- 0.1164 \sin{\left(11.04 z_{1} + 0.1144 \right)} \\[5pt] \dot{z}_{5} &= - 3.233 z_{4}- 0.1458\end{aligned} $$

The dominant linear terms form three oscillator pairs. Their frequency ratios are approximately $1:1.99:3.00$, corresponding to the vortex-shedding cycle and its second and third harmonics. Small nonlinear terms modify and couple the oscillations. These equations describe the POD coordinates of the whole field. [1]

5. Predict over the held-out interval¶

Integrate the accepted system from the first observed test state.

  • The test interval is $t=85.1$–$100.0$, spanning 14.9 time units. The solver uses elapsed time from its initial condition.
  • Later test observations are used only to assess the prediction.
  • Stable predictions over this entire interval demonstrate autonomous evolution of the discovered system.
In [8]:
test = flow["test"]
prediction = workflow.rollout(final_equation, test["t"], test["x0"])
if prediction is None:
    raise RuntimeError("The selected equation did not complete its test rollout.")
print(f"Full-interval coordinate NMSE: {workflow.nmse(test['x'], prediction):.5f}")
figures.flow_rollout(flow, prediction);
plt.show()

Full-interval coordinate NMSE: 0.06887

6. Reconstruct physical fields¶

The symbolic ODE supplies the coefficients used to rebuild the field.

  1. Undo coordinate standardization.
  2. Multiply the coefficients by the POD spatial basis.
  3. Restore the development mean field.

Compare a reconstructed symbolic prediction with the corresponding six-mode POD representation.

In [9]:
# Reconstruct one predicted field at a specified test time.
snapshot_index = 45
predicted_coordinates = prediction[snapshot_index]
observed_coordinates = flow["test"]["x"][snapshot_index]

# Undo standardization, combine spatial modes, and restore the mean field.
predicted_coefficients = predicted_coordinates * flow["scale"].ravel() + flow["center"].ravel()
observed_coefficients = observed_coordinates * flow["scale"].ravel() + flow["center"].ravel()
predicted_field = flow["mean"].ravel() + flow["basis"] @ predicted_coefficients
pod_field = flow["mean"].ravel() + flow["basis"] @ observed_coefficients
relative_error = np.linalg.norm(predicted_field - pod_field) / np.linalg.norm(pod_field)
print(f"At t = {85.1 + 0.1*snapshot_index:.1f}: relative error to six-mode POD = {relative_error:.3%}")

At t = 89.6: relative error to six-mode POD = 6.707%
In [10]:
teaching.cylinder_bridge();
plt.show()

Each row above compares recorded simulation, six-mode POD, and symbolic fields at the same labeled time. The rows show predictions at t = 92.6 and 100.0, both after initialization at t = 85.1. The comparison separates POD truncation error from symbolic prediction error.

7. Reconstruction fidelity and equation discoverability¶

These answer different questions.

  • More retained modes can preserve more field detail.
  • A discoverable ODE must also model those coordinates' evolution.
  • The validation records below compare discovery configurations up to six states.
  • The 10/20-mode reconstructions above illustrate representation choices; the symbolic models use at most six states, within the VG backbone's limit.

Optional: fresh candidate generation and refinement¶

Repeat the six-state, eight-window workflow.

  • Fresh generation uses the official pretrained ODEFormer checkpoint.
  • Refinement changes constants only; verify the proposed result again.
  • Both cells are disabled by default.
In [13]:
RUN_FRESH_DISCOVERY = False
if RUN_FRESH_DISCOVERY:
    backbone = workflow.load_backbone(beam_size=20, temperature=0.1)
    fresh_pool = workflow.generate_pool(backbone, flow["generation_windows"], seeds=flow["generation_seeds"])
    fresh_ranking = workflow.rank_pool(fresh_pool, flow["ranking_windows"])
    fresh_shortlist = fresh_ranking.iloc[:10].copy()
    fresh_local_scores = []
    for equation in fresh_shortlist.equation:
        right_side = workflow.vector_field(equation, observed_states)
        squared_difference = (right_side - observed_derivative)**2
        normalized_error = np.mean(squared_difference, axis=0) / derivative_scale
        fresh_local_scores.append(np.mean(normalized_error))
    fresh_limit = 2 * np.min(fresh_local_scores)
    fresh_rows = []
    for _, candidate in fresh_shortlist.iterrows():
        checks = workflow.verify_flow(candidate.equation, flow, fresh_limit)
        fresh_rows.append({**candidate.to_dict(), **checks})
    fresh_checked = pd.DataFrame(fresh_rows)
    fresh_selected = workflow.select_admissible(fresh_checked)
    if fresh_selected is None:
        print("No admissible equation")
    else:
        workflow.show_equation(fresh_selected.equation, name="z")
In [14]:
RUN_FRESH_REFINEMENT = False
if RUN_FRESH_REFINEMENT:
    if not RUN_FRESH_DISCOVERY or fresh_selected is None:
        raise ValueError("Run fresh discovery and select an admissible equation first.")
    optimizer = workflow.CoefficientOptimizer(fresh_selected.equation, flow["ranking_windows"])
    trial = optimizer.run(maxiter=300)
    trial_checks = workflow.verify_flow(trial, flow, fresh_limit)
    accepted = trial if trial_checks["verifier_admissible"] else fresh_selected.equation
    workflow.show_equation(accepted, name="z")
